label: Steven M. Greer
narrative: Greer built the first mass witness-aggregation project and demonstrated both its power and its limits. A practising emergency physician, he founded the Center for the Study of Extraterrestrial Intelligence in 1990 and the Disclosure Project in 1993 with the explicit aim of assembling former military and government personnel willing to testify to Congress. On 9 May 2001 he convened roughly twenty of them at the National Press Club in Washington - radar operators, missile launch officers, air traffic controllers, FAA personnel - and announced that more than four hundred had given testimony, demanding congressional hearings with subpoena power and amnesty for witnesses. The event drew heavy international coverage and produced no hearing. Its consequence for the record is twofold. First, it created a large videotaped corpus of named former personnel making specific, dated, on-the-record claims, some of which - notably the missile-facility shutdown accounts - align with the FOIA-released overflight documents from 1975. Second, Greer's subsequent trajectory into claims that outran his evidence gave the institutions he was pressuring a durable reason to treat the whole category as unserious. The Clinton White House's own UFO FOIA collection (2006-0474-F) consists in the majority of documents Greer sent it, which is a precise measure of how the material was received: filed as correspondence.
